g.title: Pulmonary veins
g.desc: Four of them, two from each lung, into the left atrium.

g.title: Aorta
g.desc: Biggest artery; leaves the left ventricle, arches to the left, then down behind the heart.

g.title: Superior vena cava
g.desc: Enters the right atrium from the top; blood from the head and arms.

g.title: Inferior vena cava
g.desc: Enters the right atrium from below; blood from the rest of the body.

g.title: Pulmonary trunk
g.desc: Leaves the right ventricle, splits into left and right pulmonary arteries; in front of the aorta.

g.title: Right atrium
g.desc: Top chamber on the patient's right, the left of the picture; receives both venae cavae.

g.title: Left atrium
g.desc: Top chamber on the patient's left; receives the pulmonary veins.

g.title: Right ventricle
g.desc: Thin-walled crescent; pumps only to the lungs, low pressure.

g.title: Left ventricle
g.desc: Wall about three times thicker than the right's; pumps to the entire body, high pressure.

g.title: Interventricular septum
g.desc: Thick wall between the ventricles; keeps deoxygenated and oxygenated blood separate.

g.title: Papillary muscles
g.desc: Stick up from the ventricle floor; pull the chordae so flaps don't blow back.

g.title: Chordae tendineae
g.desc: Cords from the edges of the AV valve flaps down to the papillary muscles.

g.title: Tricuspid valve
g.desc: AV valve between right atrium and right ventricle; three flaps.

g.title: Mitral valve
g.desc: AV valve between left atrium and left ventricle; also called bicuspid, two flaps.

g.title: Pulmonary valve
g.desc: Semilunar valve at the right ventricle's exit into the pulmonary trunk.

g.title: Aortic valve
g.desc: Semilunar valve at the left ventricle's exit into the aorta.

g.title: Apex
g.desc: Pointed bottom, the tip of the left ventricle; points down and to the left.
